coreIdea: CFG generates via rules; CFL = generated by some CFG = accepted by some PDA (one stack). One matching-pair OK (a^n b^n); three+ simultaneous matches NOT CFL (a^n b^n c^n).
mustRememberFormulas: NOT closed: ∩ of two CFLs, complement
S→aSb|ε generates a^n b^n — classic single-stack-matching CFL
DCFL ⊊ CFL (strict subset) — not every CFL has a DPDA

patternRecognitionTable.seeThis: grammar given, asked what language it generates
'is this grammar ambiguous' or 'does a DPDA exist'

commonTrapsQuickList: CFL∩CFL has NO guarantee of being CFL; CFL∩Regular ALWAYS is
Recursive-looking grammars (aS|bS|ε) are often secretly REGULAR, not requiring CFL power
Not every CFL has a DPDA — DCFL is strictly smaller
Two independent matching pairs (or three counts) in one language usually breaks CFL-ness
highYieldPyqLessons: Grammar→language identification (14/35) and CFL classification (12/35) are ~74% of this topic — master deriving short strings by hand and recognizing grammar shapes.
The single most repeated exam fact: CFL is NOT closed under intersection (of two CFLs) or complement — tested from many different angles across decades.
